formula_convention.notes: This is a monthly return-based BAB MethodSpec. The signal is estimated ex ante beta; the portfolio return is the paper's beta-neutral BAB factor return. For US equities, the main paper test uses CRSP common stocks from January 1926 through March 2012. Default return period is calendar_month; this is a return-based monthly signal, not an accounting-period signal.

paper.title: Betting against Beta
paper_sections: 3.3. Data used to test the theory's portfolio predictions
4. Betting against beta in each asset class
4.5. Betting against all of the betas

economic_intuition.value: Leverage-constrained investors overweight high-beta securities instead of using leverage, which depresses high-beta risk-adjusted returns. A BAB factor buys low-beta assets with leverage and shorts high-beta assets after de-leveraging, earning positive risk-adjusted returns if the security market line is too flat.

source.quote: Because constrained investors bid up high-beta assets, high beta is associated with low alpha.
source.interpretation: The paper links leverage constraints to low alphas for high-beta assets and motivates a long-low-beta, short-high-beta BAB portfolio.

definition.value: The firm-level sorting signal is each stock's ex ante estimated beta. The BAB factor is then constructed by going long low-beta stocks and short high-beta stocks, with both legs rescaled to beta one.

source.location: Introduction p.2; Section 3.2 p.9; Table 3 caption p.13
source.quote: long the low-beta portfolio and that shortsells the high-beta portfolio
source.interpretation: The paper uses ex ante estimated beta as the stock-level sorting signal; BAB is the portfolio factor constructed from that signal.

formula.expression: estimated_beta_i_m = 0.6 * beta_ts_i_m + 0.4 * 1; beta_ts_i_m = corr_5y_3d(excess_ret_i, excess_ret_market) * vol_1y_1d(excess_ret_i) / vol_1y_1d(excess_ret_market)
formula.paper_expression: β_i^TS = ρ_i σ_i / σ_m; β_i = w β_i^TS + (1 − w) β^XS, with w = 0.6 and β^XS = 1

source.location: Section 3.1 Estimating ex ante betas p.8; Equations (14)-(15)
source.quote: We estimate pre-ranking betas from rolling regressions of excess returns on market excess returns.
source.interpretation: The signal used to rank stocks is the paper's ex ante beta estimate, computed from rolling return volatilities/correlations and shrunk toward one.

calculation_steps.name: compute_excess_returns
calculation_steps.expression: excess_ret_i_m = ret_i_m - rf_m; excess_ret_market_m = market_ret_m - rf_m
calculation_steps.description: Convert stock and market returns into excess returns before estimating beta.

source.location: Section 3.1 Estimating ex ante betas p.8
source.quote: rolling regressions of excess returns on market excess returns
source.interpretation: Beta is estimated from stock excess returns relative to market excess returns.

calculation_steps.name: estimate_time_series_beta
calculation_steps.description: Estimate time-series beta using one-year volatility and five-year correlation; volatilities use one-day log returns, correlations use overlapping three-day log returns.

source.quote: one-year rolling standard deviation for volatilities and a five-year horizon for the correlation
source.interpretation: The paper estimates beta as correlation times the stock-to-market volatility ratio, with different windows for volatility and correlation.

calculation_steps.name: apply_beta_shrinkage
calculation_steps.description: Shrink the time-series beta estimate toward one using the paper-stated common shrinkage rule.

source.quote: we set w=0.6 and βXS=1
source.interpretation: The ex ante beta used for sorting and portfolio scaling is the shrunk beta estimate.

calculation_steps.name: apply_minimum_observation_rules
calculation_steps.expression: require min_obs(vol_daily)=120 and min_obs(corr_daily)=750; if monthly_only, require min_obs(vol_monthly)=12 and min_obs(corr_monthly)=36
calculation_steps.description: Apply the paper-stated minimum data requirements for daily beta estimation and monthly-data fallback.

source.quote: at least three years (750 trading days)
source.interpretation: The paper states minimum observations for volatility/correlation estimation; the formula step records these as calculation constraints rather than a separate BAB-specific schema field.

sign.meaning: Higher ex ante beta is associated with lower alpha and lower risk-adjusted performance. This sign refers to alpha/risk-adjusted return, not necessarily raw excess return; the BAB factor therefore goes long low-beta stocks and short high-beta stocks.

source.location: Abstract p.1; Section 4.1 Stocks pp.10-11; Table 3 p.13
source.quote: the alphas decline almost monotonically from the low-beta to high-beta portfolios
source.interpretation: The paper reports that alphas and Sharpe ratios decline from low-beta to high-beta portfolios, while raw excess returns are similar across beta portfolios. Therefore the negative sign is about abnormal/risk-adjusted return rather than a simple raw-return prediction.

source.interpretation: The paper discusses reducing beta-estimation outlier influence through shrinkage toward one, not by percentile winsorization. Therefore lower_pct and upper_pct remain null for the main BAB factor construction.

sort.role: signal ranking used to form low-beta and high-beta legs for a beta-neutral BAB factor

source.location: Section 3.2 Constructing betting against beta factors p.9; Table 3 caption p.13
source.quote: portfolio is composed of all stocks with a beta below (above) its asset class median; all stocks are assigned to one of two portfolios: low beta and high beta
source.interpretation: The paper ranks stocks by estimated beta and forms two low/high beta portfolios around the asset-class median. The ls_quantile value records this median split only; weighting_scheme remains the source of truth for the rank weights and beta rescaling.

weighting_scheme.paper_formula: wH = k(z - zbar)+; wL = k(z - zbar)-; r_BAB = (1/beta_L)(r_L - rf) - (1/beta_H)(r_H - rf)
weighting_scheme.description: Stocks are first weighted by centered beta ranks in the low-beta and high-beta legs. Each leg is then rescaled to beta one, creating a self-financing zero-beta BAB portfolio.
weighting_scheme.long_short_rule: Long the rank-weighted low-beta leg levered to beta one; short the rank-weighted high-beta leg de-levered to beta one.

source.quote: both portfolios are rescaled to have a beta of one
source.interpretation: Equations (16)-(17) define beta-rank weights and beta rescaling for the self-financing BAB factor. This is the same construction summarized in reported_results.return_calculation.portfolio_return. The paper also states that securities are weighted by ranked betas; detailed weighting evidence is consolidated here rather than duplicated in weights_source.

implied_factor_direction.note: The paper explicitly defines the BAB factor as long low-beta and short high-beta. It is a custom beta-neutral/rank-weighted factor, not a plain EW/VW high-minus-low spread.

reported_results.return_type_explanation: Monthly BAB return is the excess return of the low-beta leg rescaled by its ex ante beta minus the excess return of the high-beta leg rescaled by its ex ante beta.

comparison_policy.note: Compare backtests to the paper's low-minus-high beta-neutral BAB direction. Do not flip to high-minus-low merely because many accounting factors use high-minus-low conventions.

source.quote: Excess returns are above the US Treasury bill rate.
source.interpretation: BAB returns and alphas are computed using monthly stock excess returns relative to the Treasury bill rate. The input-return expression is monthly stock return minus the US Treasury bill rate; components are stock return and risk-free rate.

return_combination.note: Low and high legs are not EW/VW decile tails; they are rank-weighted halves rescaled by estimated leg betas. Paper-specific BAB combination formerly summarized as beta_neutral_low_minus_high_spread: rank-weighted low-beta and high-beta legs are each rescaled to beta one; final return is low-minus-high excess return.

source.location: Section 3.2 p.9; Equation (17); Table 3 caption p.13
source.quote: The betting against beta factor is a self-financing portfolio
source.interpretation: The paper gives a custom BAB construction: estimate ex ante betas, rank stocks monthly, form rank-weighted low/high beta legs, rescale each side to beta one, and compute the low-minus-high self-financing return. This is not a standard characteristic_sort dispatch because rank weighting and beta rescaling are essential.

portfolio_return.interpretation: The codegen target is the paper's US equity BAB factor: estimate ex ante betas, rank stocks monthly, form rank-weighted low/high beta legs, rescale each side to beta one, and compute the low-minus-high self-financing return.

annotator_notes:
Paper-first MethodSpec for Frazzini and Pedersen's original US equity BAB factor. The paper also contains international and multi-asset BAB factors; those are recorded as secondary specs here and can be split into separate MethodSpecs later if the project wants multi-asset backtests.
Paper-first scope note: this file intentionally scopes the multi-asset paper to the US equity BAB factor in Table 3. Do not interpret missing futures, commodities, bonds, currencies, or international-equity data fields as extraction omissions for this MethodSpec.
Signal naming note: "ex_ante_beta" is an annotator-normalized descriptive name for the paper's estimated beta signal (β̂_i); the paper's named factor is BAB.
